$comment: The numeric M1 tolerances (§18.1, §18.2, §26.1). §18.1 puts them AFTER the M0 baseline run — an effect size or a tolerance picked before the baseline shows the spread of the metric is a guess with a number attached. §26.1 makes them a V1.0 release condition: 'die numerischen M1-Toleranzen nach dem M0-Baseline-Run versioniert festgeschrieben sind'. Changing a value here means bumping registration_version and saying which version a report belongs to.
$comment_version_2: v2 (2026-08-28): false_abstention moves from not-registrable to a registered tolerance on weak_result, after faa7050 moved that predicate into core and a second run measured it. relevant_loss is unchanged.

derived_from.denominator: the 432-case main denominator of the §19 gold set — 372 answerable, 60 no-answer; the 16 probe cases are excluded (probe_group)
derived_from.$comment: One run, one arm. A tolerance derived here does not transfer to a different vault, a different embedding model or the BM25-only arm without being re-derived.

relevant_loss.unit: share of answerable cases whose expected_ids never appear in the production pool (k=10)
relevant_loss.denominator: answerable cases in the main denominator, probes excluded
relevant_loss.$comment_derivation: Measured 18.5%. The upper bound of the Wilson 95% interval is 22.8%, so any tolerance below that would fire on measurement noise alone — a clean re-run with no code change would breach it often enough to make the gate untrustworthy. 0.23 is the next round figure above the interval and marks exactly the line 'outside the noise band of the baseline'.
relevant_loss.$comment_stricter: 0.20 sits INSIDE the confidence interval and would fail runs that changed nothing.
relevant_loss.$comment_looser: 0.30 would let a real regression of more than 10pp pass — more than the entire distance between the hybrid arm and BM25-only on this set (3.2pp at Recall@3).
relevant_loss.$comment_report_separately: BINDING, and the reason the aggregate alone is not enough. Relevant loss is wildly uneven across origins: second_person (the independently working second person of §19) 37/67 = 55.2%, user_query 9/45 = 20.0%, session_transcript 23/260 = 8.8%. The aggregate of 18.5% is dominated by hook telemetry, which makes up 260 of 372 cases. A future set with a different origin mix would move the aggregate without anything in retrieval changing, and a degradation confined to the blind batch could hide entirely under the tolerance. The per-origin figures are reported next to the aggregate, never folded into it.

false_abstention.unit: share of answerable cases for which weak_result fires — no hit in the pool anchors lexically (neither matched_recall_when nor a title match)
false_abstention.denominator: answerable cases in the main denominator, probes excluded

derived_from.$comment_commit: The measured code is the working tree that became faa7050 ('weak_result zieht nach core'). The manifest of that run records git as 320e19b-dirty, because the move was not yet committed when it ran — the artifact and this field describe the same code from two sides, and neither is wrong.
derived_from.$comment: A second run on the same gold set, taken after weak_result moved to core so the gold-set runner could call the production predicate instead of reimplementing it.

false_abstention.$comment_derivation: Measured 0 of 372. With zero events the point estimate carries no information on its own, so the tolerance is set from the upper bound of the Wilson 95% interval: 1.02%. 0.015 sits 0.48pp above it — close enough that a genuine regression shows up, far enough that the interval itself does not breach the gate. Same construction as relevant_loss, only from a zero count instead of a rate.
false_abstention.$comment_stricter: 0.010 sits ON the interval bound: with 372 cases even a single false abstention is 0.27%, so a handful of them would breach a gate that the measurement cannot distinguish from the baseline.
false_abstention.$comment_looser: 0.03 would allow eleven answerable cases to be suppressed before the gate notices — against a baseline of zero, that is a regression nobody would see.

discriminance.$comment: A tolerance on a predicate that never fires would be as empty as the score floor was. These two counts are the evidence that weak_result actually discriminates: it stays silent on answerable cases and speaks on cases where there is nothing to find.
discriminance.$comment_reading: It fires on 3 of 8 nonsense probes and on 1 of 60 no-answer cases while staying silent on all 372 answerable ones. Sensitivity is clearly incomplete — 5 of 8 nonsense probes still produce a lexically anchored hit — but the direction is right and the false-positive side is clean, which is what a false-abstention tolerance is set against.

supersedes.$comment: HISTORY, kept on purpose: it explains why the mechanism was changed rather than the number tuned. Do not delete when this entry is next revised.
supersedes.why_abandoned: Abstention used to be a score floor, and on the hybrid path that floor cannot fire. The lowest possible score of a rank-1 hit is RRF_SCALE/(RRF_K+1) = 81.967 while the documented floor is 30 — unreachable by construction. The M0 baseline measured 0 of 372 false abstentions AND 0 of 60 correct abstentions: the metric was pinned at zero and would have passed any tolerance, including 0%.
supersedes.why_not_a_threshold: A score threshold does not rescue it either. The best achievable cut was measured on both arms (Youden J over every observed score): hybrid at 139.3 keeps 64.8% of answerable cases while still letting 23.3% of no-answer cases through (J=0.415); BM25-only at 2104.3 keeps only 54.0% to block 91.7% (J=0.457). Even at the optimum a third to a half of all correct answers would be suppressed — the score does not separate the two groups.
supersedes.resolved_by: faa7050 moved weak_result from packages/daemon to packages/core, so the gold-set runner calls the production predicate instead of reimplementing it.

false_abstention.$comment_open_dependency: OPEN as of 2026-08-28: a separate run is investigating WHY weak_result is silent on all 372 answerable cases — whether that is genuine precision or the predicate being too permissive (its title match is tolerant by design, and a tolerant anchor is easy to satisfy). If that investigation changes the reading, this entry is revised and registration_version bumped. The tolerance stands until then; it is derived from what was measured, not from what the measurement means.

$comment_not_registered: Only the two tolerances named in the M0 checklist are settled here. Anything else M1 may need (§18.2) waits for its own measurement — an unmeasured tolerance is a guess whether or not it sits in a versioned file.
